SPACE CRAFT JOURNAL / WALLS & MATERIALS

Creative 3D wall design ideas to transform your office space.

Choose a wall finish for more than the photograph. This Space Craft planning note looks at creative 3d wall design ideas to transform your office space through the choices that affect everyday use, the details worth testing and the questions to take into your project brief.

Space Craft editorialPlanning note · 4 min read
IN THIS NOTEUse the visual to answer a specific questionGive each surface a jobCheck the everyday contact pointsResolve what sits behind itMap activity before assigning desksBefore you decide
01 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Use the visual to answer a specific question

A 3D view can help test proportions, sightlines or a material combination. Ask which elements are accurate and which are placeholders. Check the proposal against the measured plan and the product schedule so that the image remains a useful decision aid rather than an assumed construction specification.

02 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Give each surface a job

A wall can guide visitors, provide writable space, support acoustic treatment or carry a small moment of brand identity. Decide what it needs to do before adding decorative layers.

03 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Check the everyday contact points

Review cleanability, edges, joints and likely wear around desks and circulation routes. Compare physical samples in the actual light rather than relying only on a small screen image.

04 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Resolve what sits behind it

Sockets, access panels, doors and equipment can interrupt a seemingly simple elevation. Coordinate these details early so the finish does not create an obstacle to maintenance.

05 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Map activity before assigning desks

Write down the tasks people perform, how often teams overlap and when visitors arrive. A desk count alone will not reveal the need for private calls, project tables or storage.

BEFORE YOU DECIDE

Take this into your brief.

  • Name the functional purpose of each proposed finish.
  • Compare samples beside adjacent materials.
  • Record cleaning and replacement requirements.

Write down one priority, one constraint and one question you still need to answer. Review them beside the plan or material sample before agreeing the next design decision.
